stem.en: A forecast says a storm surge will lift the sea 3.2 metres above its usual level along one stretch of coast. Village P stands 2.4 metres above sea level and village Q stands 4.0 metres above it. If the forecast is right, whose ground goes under water?

text.en: Neither, as a surge stops at the shoreline

feedback.en: A surge does not stop at the shoreline. It covers low ground, and that is why SSEWS forecasts how far the water will spread.

text.en: Both, as the surge covers the whole coast

feedback.en: Compare the heights. The sea at 3.2 metres stays below village Q's ground at 4.0 metres.

text.en: Only village Q, as the surge hits high ground

feedback.en: Water covers the lower ground first. Village Q is the higher of the two.

text.en: Only village P, as the sea rises above it

feedback.en: Yes. 3.2 metres is above P's ground at 2.4 metres and below Q's at 4.0 metres.

explanation.en: Ground goes under water when the sea rises above it. Here that is village P, at 2.4 metres. A forecast can be off, so everyone told to evacuate should still go, even from ground that looks high enough.

hints.en: Compare each village's height with the height of the water.
